memos.headline: S04 and S06 Lead on Relative Strength; S02 in Freefall, S05 and S08 Weak
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation across the universe as of May 9. S04 is the standout leader—up 15% over 4 weeks, trading 12.4% above its 50-day and 6% above its 200-day mean, with the strongest relative strength vs SPY at +7.5% (4w) and +13.7% (12w), though RSI at 71.9 flags overbought risk near-term. S06 is the second-best structure: only 9.6% off its 52w high, above both moving averages, with positive 26w returns of +12.8% and moderate RSI of 61.2. On the avoid side, S02 is in a technical crash—down 36% over 4 weeks, RSI at 23.6, sitting 29.6% below its 200-day mean and 39.1% off its high; I see no reason to step in front of that. S05 and S08 are also weak, both well below key averages with negative relative strength, though not as extreme as S02. I would need S02 to reclaim its 50-day mean (roughly ~485) and S04 to hold above 410 (approximately its 50-day) to maintain my current views.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+13.7% vs SPY 12w), above both moving averages, but RSI 71.9 warrants watching for a pullback to ~410 (50d area) as a stop level.
Closest to 52w high at -9.6%, above both 50d and 200d means, positive 26w return of +12.8%, and manageable RSI of 61.2; would reassess below 240.
RSI 23.6 and -36% over 4 weeks with -43.5% relative strength vs SPY screams capitulation still in progress; no technical base visible yet.
Down 26% from 52w high, 10.7% below 200d mean, negative relative strength of -7.6% (4w) and -10.3% (12w); would need a close above 160 to reconsider.
Trading 12.3% below 200d mean with -9.7% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks; trend is clearly down until price reclaims ~210 area.
Strong 4w bounce of +12.6% but still 8.8% below 200d mean and 21.9% off highs; needs to clear ~340 to confirm trend reversal.
RSI 50.6 and flat 12w return suggest a range-bound name with no clear directional edge; watching for a break above 115 or below 100.
Modest bounce to near 50d mean but still 20% off highs and underperforming SPY by 9.2% over 12 weeks; no strong conviction either way.
Bouncing with +8.4% over 4w but still 6.7% below 200d mean and 21.9% off highs; high ATR of 3.58% adds risk—need a close above 125 for conviction.
RSI 38.2, 6.5% below 200d mean, and -11.2% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks; persistent underperformance with no sign of a bottom yet.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Earnings Power; S07 and S09 Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I screened the latest filings across the universe and the dispersion in earnings quality is striking. S10 posted 56.2% net margins on 77.9% YoY revenue growth with only $8.46B in total debt—the cleanest balance sheet and strongest operating leverage in the group. S05 delivered $34.54B in net income on $90.23B revenue (38.3% margin) with net income up 46% YoY and minimal debt of $14.79B, which is durable earnings power I'm willing to pay for. On the other end, S07 saw revenue decline 9.8% YoY and net income collapse 29.8% to $2.00B on a 14.1% margin burdened by $31.74B in debt—classic cash-flow compression I want to avoid. S09 is similarly concerning: flat revenue (+0.1%), declining net income (-6.2%), and a thin 9.3% margin with $32.82B in debt, suggesting limited pricing power and rising cost pressure.

views.note: 56.2% net margin, ~80% YoY revenue and earnings growth, and only $8.46B debt make this the highest-quality earnings stream in the universe; a sustained margin decline below 40% would change my view.
38.3% net margin with 46% YoY net income growth and just $14.79B debt signals durable, expanding earnings power; I'd reassess if margins compress below 30%.
36.9% net margin and 17.7% YoY net income growth on $70B revenue with manageable $42.88B debt is strong, though slightly lower conviction given heavier debt load than S10/S05.
Revenue of $155.67B growing 8.6% YoY and a 64.2% jump in net income are encouraging, but the 11.0% net margin and $58.75B debt leave limited margin of safety if growth slows.
$95.36B revenue with 26% margin is solid but only 5.1% top-line growth and $92.20B in total debt suggest mature, leveraged earnings; I need to see re-acceleration to get constructive.
32.3% margin and 8.1% revenue growth are respectable, but $407.22B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe and makes earnings highly sensitive to funding costs.
Flat revenue (+0.1%), declining net income (-6.2%), a thin 9.3% margin, and $32.82B debt point to deteriorating earnings power; I'd reconsider only if margins recover above 12%.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY with $31.74B debt against only $14.25B quarterly revenue is textbook cash-flow compression I refuse to own.
9.8% revenue growth is decent but a 5.7% net margin on $109.58B revenue with $81.27B debt and unavailable YoY net income comparison leave too many unknowns for conviction.
19.1% margin is healthy but revenue declined 2.1% YoY and net income was essentially flat (+0.4%), suggesting stagnation; $24.25B debt is manageable but growth needs to inflect.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market and Steepening Curve — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Lean Into Banks
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, CPI is running at 2.4% y/y (manageable but sticky), and unemployment has crept up 30bp over the past year to 4.2%, signaling a mild labor market softening. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+83bp y/y to +0.47pp), which historically benefits banks' net interest margins and signals the market is pricing eventual easing. The 10y yield at 4.37% is down 12bp over three months, providing a modest tailwind for duration-sensitive equities. I have moderate conviction in this pause-to-easing transition but would reassess if the next CPI print re-accelerates above 3% y/y or if unemployment reverses below 4.0%, either of which would reset the regime call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from the 10y yield drifting lower and a Fed on hold leaning toward eventual easing.
Banks gain from a steepening 10y-2y curve (+83bp y/y) which supports net interest margin expansion.
Staples offer defensive positioning but limited upside in a pause regime where growth is softening only mildly.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+0.20 over 3m) but the curve steepening keeps recession risk contained for now.
Energy tends to underperform in a late-cycle slowdown with softening labor demand and no imminent policy stimulus.
Growth-oriented sector should benefit from declining long-end yields and a Fed that is done hiking.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S04 and S06 Positive Momentum vs. S02 and S08 Negative Tone Shifts
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in post-earnings sentiment across the universe. S04 posted a +7.6% price reaction on its 4/30 results, the strongest positive signal in the group, and that enthusiasm likely has not fully dissipated. S06 similarly rallied +4.0% on 4/11 earnings with follow-on Reg FD and Other Events filings suggesting continued narrative building. On the negative side, S02's -22.4% collapse on 4/17 earnings followed by a director departure on 4/29 signals a deeply impaired narrative that may still be deteriorating. S08 dropped -3.7% on its 5/1 results with no offsetting positive filings, and S01 also fell -3.7% on 4/24 earnings though a subsequent 5/1 Other Events filing could indicate management is trying to stabilize the story. I have highest conviction on the extremes—S04 long and S02 avoid—and less conviction on names where price reactions were muted (S03, S07, S09).

views.note: Strongest post-earnings price reaction in the universe at +7.6%, suggesting a positive narrative shift that may carry further.
Earnings-day +4.0% pop and high filing cadence (4 filings in April) suggest sustained positive attention and narrative momentum.
A -22.4% earnings reaction followed by a director departure 12 days later points to a deeply negative and potentially worsening sentiment trajectory.
Earnings-day -3.7% decline with no subsequent positive filings to offset; tone appears to be drifting negative with no catalyst for reversal.
Earnings drop of -3.7% was notable but a follow-on Other Events filing on 5/1 and steady dividend disclosure may stabilize sentiment; watching for direction.
Positive +1.7% earnings reaction and unusually high filing volume (5 filings since mid-March) suggest building narrative interest, though the moves are modest.
Muted +0.6% earnings reaction and two director change filings create ambiguity; sentiment is flat with no clear directional signal.
Earnings reaction of +0.4% is essentially flat; director change and Reg FD filings in early April add noise but no clear sentiment trend.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Weak Oil Signal Persistent Geopolitical Headwinds Despite VIX Compression
memos.body: I note that while the VIX has collapsed 57% over the past month to 22.48, the economic policy uncertainty index remains stubbornly elevated at 567.82, essentially flat month-over-month and still reflecting a structurally uncertain policy environment around trade, sanctions, and export controls. HY spreads at 3.51% have tightened 106bp in a month but remain 84bp wider than three months ago, suggesting credit markets are pricing residual tail risk. WTI crude at $61.25 is down 14.1% over three months, consistent with demand destruction fears tied to tariff escalation and China slowdown concerns rather than a supply glut. S05 stands out with five 8-K filings since mid-March—an unusually high cadence of 'Other Events' disclosures that may reflect supply-chain or regulatory repositioning—while S06 and S01 also show elevated disclosure activity in April, potentially linked to policy-driven operational adjustments. I have moderate conviction that names with heavy China/trade exposure face structural headwinds until we see a concrete de-escalation in tariff or export-control policy.

views.note: Unusually high 8-K cadence (five filings in seven weeks) suggests ongoing material policy or supply-chain disruptions that management is navigating in real time.
Three 8-K filings in April hint at policy-related disclosures, but without content detail I cannot distinguish routine from material geopolitical risk.
Three filings across April-May suggest active investor communication amid policy uncertainty; the flat EPU index keeps me from taking a directional stance.
Two Reg FD disclosures and one Other Events filing in April-May are consistent with proactive guidance updates but insufficient to gauge geopolitical exposure.
Single mid-April 8-K provides minimal signal; WTI weakness and elevated policy uncertainty warrant monitoring but not a directional call.
Only one Reg FD filing and no cluster of disclosures suggests relative insulation from the policy turbulence affecting peers; low conviction given limited data.

plans.rationale: Strongest consensus across all analysts: best relative strength (+13.7% vs SPY 12w), 36.9% net margin with 17.7% earnings growth, and the strongest post-earnings sentiment pop (+7.6%). Technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysts all rate it a high-conviction long. RSI at 71.9 is the only caution, so I size to max but use a tight stop near the 50d mean.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 410 (approximate 50-day mean) would break the uptrend structure and invalidate the momentum thesis.

plans.rationale: Second-best technical structure (closest to 52w high, above both MAs, RSI 61.2) with positive sentiment momentum (+4.0% earnings reaction and high filing cadence). Fundamentals analyst is neutral due to massive $407B debt load, so I size slightly below S04. Geopolitics analyst also neutral, no red flag.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 240 would put it below both moving averages and negate the relative-strength thesis.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst's top pick with 56.2% net margin and ~80% revenue growth on a clean balance sheet. Technical analyst is neutral (still 6.7% below 200d, high ATR), so I size down and use a wider stop. No negative sentiment or geopolitical flags. The earnings quality justifies holding through near-term volatility.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below 105 (roughly 10% stop) or net margin compressing below 40% in next filing would invalidate the thesis.

plans.rationale: Modest support from macro analyst (benefits from lower long-end yields, Fed done hiking) and geopolitics analyst (relatively insulated from policy turbulence). Fundamentals show 64.2% net income growth though margins are thin at 11%. Technical analyst is neutral. Low conviction warrants small size.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 178 (roughly 8% stop, near recent lows) or a re-acceleration in CPI above 3% y/y would prompt exit.
